records.title: Buy Original Irish Art
records.standfirst: How an Irish homeowner finds, chooses, commissions and lives with original work by a local artist. Where to look, what to agree before buying, and how to get the size right.

records.title: Above and Beyond
records.standfirst: You do not need a tree to build above your garden, and Ireland already sells it from a few hundred euro. What decides the result is a number almost nobody mentions.

records.title: Driveway Income
records.standfirst: An under-used driveway is worth what its location is worth. What Irish homeowners actually earn, what planning, tax and insurance require, and why nobody here has answered the planning question yet.

records.title: Garden Retreat
records.standfirst: An ordinary garden may already contain somewhere to retreat to. Three routes sold in Ireland with published prices — a compact sauna, a wood-fired hot tub and a cold plunge — and what each one actually asks of a garden.

records.title: The Hidden Bins
records.standfirst: Ordinary domestic wheelie bins can be stored below ground and raised when they are needed. Proven residential systems in Britain and Germany, and where Ireland stands.

records.title: Hidden Cars
records.standfirst: Stacked, lowered and concealed parking: ways to hold two cars in the space normally used by one. What Irish planning allows, what the ground decides, and what it costs to do properly.

records.title: Home Exchange
records.standfirst: A home standing empty can be exchanged for the use of somebody else’s. What that means in Ireland, where the new short-term letting rules sit, and the questions to settle first.

records.title: The House as a Power Station
records.standfirst: Computing cannot stop making heat, and a house cannot stop needing it. What is already happening elsewhere, what is already happening in Tallaght, and what an Irish property can actually do today.

records.title: What Could You Build in Your Garden?
records.standfirst: A separate building at the end of your own garden: an office, a studio, a room for the kids — or, since July 2026, a detached home of 32 to 45 m² as exempted development. What the rules are, and whether your garden has room.

records.title: The Neighbourhood Parcel House
records.standfirst: A few homes on every road are better placed than the rest to take in a parcel. What an Irish household can do today, what it takes on, and what is not available here yet.

records.title: Open Your Home to Art
records.standfirst: Space in an Irish home, and an artist with finished work and nowhere to put it: what you could offer, what to agree, and what your insurer needs to know. An exhibition is optional.

records.title: The Borrowed Garden
records.standfirst: Lending a small part of an Irish garden to somebody nearby who wants to grow food: what you decide, what to agree, and why keeping your own access keeps it your garden.

records.title: Your Home On Screen
records.standfirst: Some productions are not looking for a remarkable house. They are looking for an ordinary one, on an ordinary street. What Irish film, television, advertising and content productions actually look for in a home.
